title: Onramp Labs: Inline Scenario Quickstarts for Console Empty States
creator: Aisha Kapoor
summary: Design a set of lightweight, runnable "labs" surfaced inside empty-state canvases across Console (Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost views) to teach common tasks with one-click scaffolding and inline guidance.
description: Problem: New users reach Console empty states (no dashboards, no rollouts, no cost data) and leave because they don’t know the next concrete step. Goal: Ship composable inline 'Onramp Labs'—small, focused scenario templates that users can run in-place to see outcomes, learn a workflow, and seed example data or configurations. Labs should be modular, accessible, instrumentable, and low-friction (try-with-one-click + guided microsteps). This ticket covers design exploration, prototype, accessibility pass, and handoff-ready specs for engineering.
tasks: Run exploratory workshop with PM/Eng to map high-value starter scenarios for Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost views
Create 3 high-fidelity prototypes in Figma: Dashboard Lab (seed example widget + query), Rollout Lab (canary deploy walkthrough), Cost Lab (budget discovery + cost card)
Define microcopy, success states, and 'undo' flows for seeded artifacts
Design keyboard-only and screen-reader flows; produce A11Y checklist
Design analytics events and success metrics for lab completion and CTA engagement
Draft engineering handoff with interaction specs, edge cases, and fallback behaviour
acceptance_criteria: Prototypes validated in 5 usability sessions with ≥80% completion rate for first-time users
Figma spec contains annotated interactions, microcopy, error states, and accessibility notes
List of seed contents and sizes for each lab (e.g., dashboard widgets, sample traces) agreed with Eng
Event taxonomy agreed for instrumentation: lab_shown, lab_started, lab_completed, lab_skipped
Handoff doc + PR template created in Confluence and linked to the ticket
design_notes: Keep labs under 3 micro-steps; prioritize 'do then learn' pattern vs long tutorials
Use subtle affordances (ghost cards, coachmark overlays) rather than modal interruptions
Seeded artifacts must be clearly labeled as examples and removable with a single action
Fallback path for orgs with no permission to seed resources: guided preview and 'copy config' CTA
Cost Lab must avoid sending PII; use synthetic cost samples with realistic distributions
progress_updates: 2026-02-25: Workshop completed with PM (Sofia Liu), Eng lead (Ben Carter), and Product Ops; prioritized Dashboard and Cost labs first
2026-03-01: Low-fi flows sketched; preferred pattern is inline 'panel insertion' rather than full-page wizards to reduce context switching
2026-03-05: Prototype v1 (Dashboard Lab) created in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/onramp-labs-v1; shared with Eng for feasibility notes
2026-03-07: Feasibility sync — Eng asked to limit seeded data size and provide a 'dry-run' API for orgs with strict audit policies
2026-03-10: Accessibility review meeting — added visible focus states, ARIA labels for coachmarks, and screen-reader text for seeded items
review_feedback: PM Sofia: prefer shorter lab descriptions and explicit next-step CTAs; remove jargon from microcopy
Eng Ben: requested clear idempotency contract for seed operation and retry behaviour documented
Design lead Noor: unify visual treatment with Console hint strip system; avoid new color tokens
Research: test alternate CTA verbs ("Try", "Run", "Seed") in next round to measure friction
Legal: flagged telemetry payloads; ensure no sensitive org identifiers are leaked in lab events
next_steps: Iterate prototypes with shortened microcopy and two CTA variants
Run 5 moderated tests with target personas (engineer, platform owner) week of 2026-03-15
Handoff technical spec to Eng (include seed payload limits and dry-run flag) by 2026-03-17
Coordinate with Observability team to add lab events to telemetry pipeline
